item.title: Christian Pulisic sends message with double vs. Haiti in USMNT return
item.description: MIAMI — Next week, the U.S. men's national team will no longer be Mauricio Pochettino's team . The manager is headed to take over Manchester United , returning to the Premier League where he led Tottenham Hostpur and Chelsea before. A new USMNT manager will be named. It could be someone as famous as Pep Guardiola. It may be someone known mostly to hardcore soccer fans. That manager will call in Christian Pulisic. He will still be there, and he'll be there for the next manager, too. The national team belongs to everyone, but every nation has its eras. Pulisic's started early, when he was the young hotshot on a team that missed the 2018 World Cup. He has passed from the great hope to the hero to ... whatever he is now. But he is part of the U.S. national team's present, and he's part of its future. He reminded fans of that Friday, Nov. 14 with a Man of the Match showing in a 6-0 romp over Haiti . This was not a friendly. The Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series started Friday and will be decided Tuesday, Nov. 17. Except it was all but decided in the second half at Nu Stadium, with Pulisic helping to set up Julian Hall's goal to make it 2-0 in the 52nd minute, then scored two goals of his own − one from the penalty spot in the 62nd and another in the 63rd as soon as play resumed. Barely 100 seconds later, Pulisic gets a second ⚡ pic.twitter.com/UjhMvhajiE — B/R Football (@brfootball) November 14, 2026 "Right after the goal I think it opened up a little bit. I got a ball with space, and kind of looked around and didn’t see many good options and felt I could curl it in to the near post. That was it. I was feeling good, so yeah," he said. Yeah. Pulisic, Weston McKennie, Folarin Balogun and a few other vets missed out on the September-October window in which the U.S. played four friendly matches. Pochettino had the regulars stay with their clubs while obviously pressing the restart button and calling in talented teenagers. "Thank you to Christian, thank you to Weston," Pochettino said. "They didn't participate in the last camp because we had half the squad made up of young kids. The way they were from the beginning was amazing. I think we can only say thank you." Pulisic and Pochettino never seemed to have the closest relationship, with the player's decision not to play in the 2025 Gold Cup baffling the manager. When Pochettino was a player, any call from Argentina was sacred. Missing a continental championship was anathema. Pulisic didn't see it that way, hoping to come in for pre-tournament friendly matches before getting a rest during the tournament proper "I think we had some good moments and he brought a lot of excitement to the team," Pulisic said when asked what Pochettino's legacy would be with the U.S. "I think he'll leave that behind." item.title: ESPN announces decision on Rex Ryan after arrest
item.description: Rex Ryan Former NFL head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan is facing six charges in connection with an alleged hit-and-run in Nashville. But it doesn’t sound like he will be missing any time on ESPN. The network says the former New York Jets head coach is still set to appear as scheduled this weekend, including on Sunday NFL Countdown , despite his arrest and the pending charges. Rex Ryan’s Alleged Hit-and-Run Police say Ryan struck two pedestrians with his pickup truck in a crosswalk on Broadway in downtown Nashville just before midnight on Nov. 5. After reviewing surveillance footage, police filed six warrants against him. The charges include leaving the scene of an accident, failure to give information or render aid, and failure to obey a traffic control signal. Ryan turned himself in on Wednesday, was released on a $6,000 bond, and is due in court on Dec. 18. One of the alleged victims, attorney Michael Holland, said Ryan “almost killed” him and his wife. He claimed Ryan ran over both of their feet, confronted them when they caught up to him in traffic, and then drove off. “He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off,” Holland said, via the New York Post. Ryan’s attorney declined to comment on the allegations. ‘As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled’ Despite the charges, ESPN doesn’t appear to be making any changes. A network spokesperson told Richard Deitsch that Ryan will make his appearance as planned on Sunday morning. “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown,” the spokesperson said, via Deitsch . Deitsch added that he “would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air.” Ryan has been an analyst at ESPN since 2017, appearing regularly on Sunday NFL Countdown and Get Up . The words “as of now” obviously leave room for things to change. But for this Sunday, at least, it sounds like Ryan will remain on the air for the network despite the incident. item.title: Notre Dame Women’s Basketball: Irish roll in 108-84 win over DePaul
item.description: Hannah Hidalgo and her friends at Notre Dame are averaging over 100 points per game the season, and that held true against DePaul on Saturday in the Shamrock Classic, 108-84. Hardy, Hidalgo Make History In No. 13 Notre Dame’s 108-84 Win Over DePaul SOUTH BEND, Ind. – Notre Dame (4-0) continued its winning ways on Saturday, as the 13th-ranked Irish downed DePaul 108-84 in the 2026 SoFi Shamrock Classic. Hannah Hidalgo paced the game with 31 points, seven rebounds and four steals. Her swipes give her 500 in her career, and she is now the only college basketball player — men’s or women’s — in history to have 2500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists and 500 steals. Anaya Hardy also notched a line in the record books, as she had a career-high 16 rebounds, including a program-record 12 offensive boards. Hardy (13), Leah Macy (24), Jacy Abii (18) and Madison St. Rose (16) also scored in double-figures. As a team, Notre Dame scored 100 points for the third consecutive game, which has not been done in the history of the storied program. HOW IT HAPPENED: The Irish offense started slow by recent standards; Hidalgo had a pair of driving layups as Notre Dame’s first two baskets from the floor on the day. DePaul then went on a 6-0 run to take a 9-5 lead into the first media break. Hidalgo had seven of Notre Dame’s first eight points. The Irish used their size to take over in the paint, as 20 of the team’s 24 first quarter points came inside. Hidalgo finished the frame with nine points, and Abii followed with seven points, four rebounds and a pair of blocks.The Irish held a 24-17 lead after 10 minutes. DePaul went on a 7-0 run to start the second quarter, while Notre Dame couldn’t find the basket, going through a 1-10 drought. The Blue Demons had four different players hit a bucket in that period, and it was 33-29 at the media break. A Hardy floater ended the drought, and DePaul was on a drought of its own with one basket in its next seven tries. Notre Dame, meanwhile, started to heat up from deep, as Hidalgo and Macy hit back-to-back triples. Macy’s basket was the first three-pointer of her Notre Dame career. Overall, Notre Dame went on a 13-2 run from 7:03 to 2:59 as the half wound down. At the end of the half, Notre Dame held a 49-34 lead. The Irish dominated on the boards, out rebounding DePaul 32-21, and scoring 13 second chance points. Individually, Hidalgo led all scorers with 19 points. Abii had seven points and seven rebounds, and Hardy led all players with nine boards, six of them offensive. Hidalgo opened the second-half scoring with a three countered by a DePaul three. The Blue Demons then failed to score for 2:43, during which the Irish started to work in transition. Macy had a pair of fast break conversions with a Hardy put-back sandwiched between. Notre Dame widened the lead to its largest of the day, 60-41, but the Blue Demons wouldn’t go away. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Stanford Cardinal flew across the country to cold, windy Blacksburg, Virginia, and took it to the Virginia Tech Hokies, defeating them 40-22. It was Stanford’s first road win since Sept. 2024. Things started badly for the Hokies early. After gaining around 34 yards on the opening drive, head coach James Franklin went for it on fourth down, and the Hokies couldn’t convert. Stanford ball. Fortunately, Tech’s defense looked like it came to play early with a couple of stops on the Cardinal’s first two drives. However, everything changed on VT’s second drive, when quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer threw an interception after his pass was tipped a few times. While the defense got another stop, Grunkemeyer was intercepted again on the next drive, this time deep in Stanford territory. The Cardinal then went on a 6-play, 78-yard drive and never looked back. After the score, Virginia Tech wide receiver Que’Sean Brown was hit and fumbled. Stanford ball again. This time, the Cardinal would start the drive on VT’s 29-yard line and scored four plays later. Suddenly, it was 21-0. Lane Stadium was shocked. So was Virginia Tech’s sideline. On their next drive, the Hokies leaned on freshman running back Jeffrey Overton Jr., who didn’t disappoint. Overton dominated the drive and scored a touchdown to make it 21-7. Unfortunately, Brent Pry’s defense would allow Stanford another field goal before halftime. Down 24-7, the Hokies opened the second half with the football. It didn’t matter. They turned it over on four downs on four plays. After a defensive stop, there was some hope when true freshman wide receiver Davion Brown took a Grunkemeyer throw and raced 69 yards to the end zone for a touchdown, making it 24-14 in the third quarter. Suddenly, there was life in Blacksburg. Too bad the defense gave it right back, failing to get stops on third and fourth downs. The Cardinal ultimately settled for a field goal, but the Hokies had no answer, punting on their next drive. Stanford responded with another field goal, followed by another Hokies’ punt. item.description: Credit: ESPN ESPN analyst and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to authorities and was arrested in Nashville on Wednesday after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his pickup truck and leaving the scene earlier this month. Just days later, it seems that Ryan will still appear on ESPN’s programming, including Sunday’s edition (10 a.m. ET) of the network’s NFL pregame show, Sunday NFL Countdown . ESPN released a statement on Saturday night saying, “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown .” From an ESPN spokesperson on Rex Ryan: “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 15, 2026 According to Nashville police , the pedestrians were crossing Broadway Street with a walk sign when Ryan turned right before “running over both victims’ feet,” along with “making contact with one of the individuals’ legs.” Ryan allegedly kept driving, but the victims caught up to him at a red light. “They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away,” per the police statement. The former head coach of the New York Jets (2009-14) and Buffalo Bills (2015-16) faces six misdemeanors: two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal. After the news of Ryan’s arrest emerged on Wednesday, ESPN issued the following statement when reached by Awful Announcing for comment: “We are aware and are in touch with Rex.” Ryan, 63, has been an analyst on ESPN since 2017 and stars on Sunday NFL Countdown alongside Mike Greenberg, Randy Moss, Alex Smith, Tedy Bruschi, and Adam Schefter. Take it from Fisch: It may be slow going for Pat Fitzgerald to turn around Michigan State, but he’s convinced the first-year Spartan coach can lead a revival. “He knows what it’s going to take, and there’s ups and downs when you’re building a program,” Fisch said. “Whether what we did at Arizona, or coming here and we had 21 starters gone from the year before we got here. Multiple starters left injured including quarterback Alessio Milivojevic , one of at least 18 one-time starters injured at some point this season. item.title: Paul Schacherer, Mark Romano goals lift UNF to ASUN men's soccer title
item.description: The last University of North Florida soccer player to score in the 2025 ASUN Championship game was the first to score in this year's title game. And the clinching goal came from an Ospreys legacy who completed a First Coast pass-and-shoot combination that ensured UNF would make more history. Senior Paul Schacherer headed the ball in the net in the 10th minute and the Ospreys held on in a gritty, chippy game until senior Mark Romano, a Ponte Vedra High graduate, took a pass from sophomore Omar Trto, a Mandarin High graduate and launched a missile into the net with 6:38 left to give top-seeded North Florida a 2-0 victory over No. 6 Queens on Nov. 14 at Hodges Stadium. The victory gave UNF (13-4-3) its third ASUN title in a row and the school record for victories in one season. First-year coach Marlon Montanella, an assistant under Jamie Davies in 2024 and 2025, becomes the third UNF coach to win an ASUN title. The Ospreys matched last year's record of nine shutouts and fifth-year senior goalkeeper Luciano Natoli recorded his seventh shutout of the season. "This team has something special to it," Montanella said. "I think this team is more mature, more experienced than the last two years and it reflects in the results. This team ... I keep telling them, they can break any record. It's a special team." UNF will find out NCAA opponent on Nov. 16 One of those records would be a first-ever NCAA Tournament victory . The Ospreys, who are 9-1-1 at home this year, will find out their opponent for the first round on Nov. 16 during the NCAA Men's Soccer Selection Show, streamed on ncaa.org at 1 p.m. Schacherer scored the winning goal in overtime last year to give UNF a 3-2 victory over Bellarmine, on a header off a throw-in. He opened the scoring against the Royals (6-11-3) nearly the same way when Tyler Prebenda threw the ball in from the right side, with the ball deflected for assists by senior midfielder and tournament MVP Anton Khelil and freshman forward Emir Trto, also a Mandarin graduate. Schacherer then glanced the ball into the net with another header for his first goal of the season. After that, it was nearly 75 long, grueling minutes before Romano struck for his team-high eighth goal of the season. Omar Trto had the ball in the middle of the pitch and fed Romano on the right, leading him perfectly. Romano ran five steps to the top of the box, touching the ball only once, then slammed it into the left corner of the net, past keeper Matthew Bademian. item.title: Fort Defiance volleyball sweeps Amelia to reach state semifinals
item.description: FORT DEFIANCE — Fort Defiance is one step away from returning to the Class 2 state volleyball championship for a third year in a row. Fort beat Amelia with relative ease 25-6, 25-14, 25-13 Saturday, Nov. 14 to advance to the state semifinals where it will play Madison County, a team Fort just beat for the regional title earlier this week. Fort hosts Madison Nov. 17. A win there and Fort would play in Salem for the state championship Nov. 21. Fort has reached, and lost, the state championship in 2024 and 2025. In the postseason, Fort has made quick work of Clarke, Madison and now Amelia to get to this point, sweeping all three. Fort coach Amber Pitsenbarger has just seen her team's confidence swell now that playoffs have started. More: Fitzgerald leads Riverheads; Fort gets first playoff win in 23 years More: Fort Defiance football celebrates historic playoff win 24 years in the making "That's been the one thing I've been trying to instill in them again, that they are all good players and we have so much depth, playing confident is what we've been really good at," she said. "Everybody lifts each other up if we make mistakes. I feel like we just have that really good team chemistry since we got in the postseason." It was the usual suspects against Amelia. Fort's Caroline Hanger, the Region 2B player of the year, had 13 kills, 10 digs and three aces. Harper Carter and Maddie Gale both had seven kills. Gale added 24 assists and 10 digs for another all-around solid game by the freshman. Libero Norah Anderson finished with 11 digs. Asked what was clicking for this team now, senior Livia Clinedinst said it was the hitting. "We have hitters everywhere," she said. "We've been working so hard in practice every day to perfect our hitting, seeing the block and just being able to hit no matter what." Hanger is the leader in kills this year with 272, but Carter, Gale and Clinedinst all have triple digits with Carter closing in on 200. And in fewer sets played, Annalee Halterman and Amelia Good both are averaging 1.5 kills a set. It's hard for defenses to focus on just one hitter. Hanger, a junior, said she has seen a drive in the senior players as they near the end of their high school volleyball careers. "They just want to be at the top, all of them want it so bad," she said. "I can just see it in all of them and that makes me want to work even harder for them." Clinedinst said she realizes that every game now can be her last on a volleyball court. Senior Alexis Miller agreed, but she said this group of seniors is so motivated to finally win a championship. "Everything is just starting to click now," Miller said. "This is a good time to peak." item.title: JJ Redick delivers major Luka Doncic news ahead of Lakers’ Phoenix Suns clash
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images JJ Redick has delivered encouraging news on Luka Doncic ahead of the Los Angeles Lakers’ meeting with the Phoenix Suns, with the Slovenian star expected to be available after an ankle scare. Doncic left the Lakers’ 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks after appearing to hurt his right ankle in the fourth quarter. However, the latest injury report has provided a major boost, with the 27-year-old not listed among the players dealing with injuries. Austin Reaves will not be as fortunate. The Lakers guard has been ruled out with a bruised left heel after also exiting the Bucks game. Luka Doncic expected to play as Los Angeles Lakers prepare for Austin Reaves absence Redick had already offered reassurance about Doncic when the Lakers returned to practice, suggesting the injury was not a major concern. “Luka is fine,” the Lakers head coach said . “The expectation would be he’s available.” The latest report has reinforced that assessment, giving Los Angeles a significant boost as it looks to extend its seven-game winning streak. Doncic has been outstanding this season, leading the NBA with 38.6 points per game while adding 7.6 assists and 7.5 rebounds. He also recorded 32 points, five rebounds and five assists before leaving against Milwaukee. However, Reaves’ absence will place more responsibility on the Slovenian guard. The pair have combined to average 63.3 points per game, making them central to the Lakers’ impressive 11-2 start. Reaves is averaging 24.7 points and 4.7 assists this season. Although initial X-rays on his heel were negative, the Lakers have opted to give him additional recovery time. Collin Sexton is also questionable after suffering a right orbital laceration against Milwaukee, while Bronny James is dealing with an illness. With Doncic expected to feature, the Lakers will have their leading scorer available against a Phoenix side led by Devin Booker. Redick will nevertheless need contributions from the supporting cast if Los Angeles is to cope without one of its most important offensive players. item.title: Hawkeyes roll past Purdue to improve to 8-2
item.description: Hank Brown threw for a touchdown and ran for another, LJ Phillips rushed for 123 yards and No. 16 Iowa beat Purdue 28-7 on Saturday night. The Hawkeyes (8-2, 5-2 Big Ten) won their third consecutive game behind an offense that had 434 yards and a defense that held the Boilermakers (3-7, 2-5) to their lowest points total of the season. Brown had a 1-yard touchdown run to open the scoring for Iowa, then threw a short pass that Braeden Jackson turned into a 44-yard touchdown late in the first half that gave the Hawkeyes a 21-7 halftime lead. Phillips had his second consecutive 100-yard rushing game. He had 128 yards in Iowa’s 24-10 win over Northwestern last Saturday. Tony Diaz had a 14-yard touchdown run for the Hawkeyes in the second quarter, and running back Xavier Williams had a 48-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Purdue’s lone scoring play came with 1:49 left in the second quarter, when quarterback Ryan Browne threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to tight end George Burhenn. Brown was 20 of 29 passing for 188 yards. Takeaways Purdue: The Boilermakers’ defensive struggles continued. Purdue came into the game 99th nationally in rushing defense and 123rd in scoring defense, and gave up 246 rushing yards to the Hawkeyes. It was the fourth consecutive loss for the Boilermakers, who haven’t won since a 41-13 victory over Minnesota on Oct. 10. Iowa: The Hawkeyes’ quest for a spot in the College Football Playoff continued with another impressive defensive performance. It was the fourth game this season in which Iowa, which ranks third in the nation in scoring defense, allowed single digits in points. Iowa’s rushing defense, which ranks fifth nationally, held Purdue to 99 yard rushing. Up next Purdue: Hosts Wisconsin next Saturday. Iowa: At Illinois next Saturday. item.title: Fleury, Murphy among Pittsburgh Penguins Hall of Fame Class of 2026
item.description: Marc-Andre Fleury, Larry Murphy, Jim Rutherford and Jack McGregor, represented by his family, were inducted into the Pittsburgh Penguins' Hall of Fame Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. The Pittsburgh Penguins have inducted their 2026 Hall of Fame class, which includes one of the most beloved goaltenders in the team’s history. Marc-André Fleury, Larry Murphy, Jim Rutherford and the family of Jack McGregor received the honor at PPG Paints Arena Saturday night before the Penguins took on the Ottawa Senators. For thousands, it was a very special “hockey night in Pittsburgh,” as crowds gave a standing ovation for some of the best to ever take the ice wearing the Penguins jersey or those who helped to build the teams behind-the-scenes. It was an emotional night for goaltender Marc-André Fleury, a three-time Stanley Cup winner who received a unanimous vote into this year’s class of inductees. “The organization gave me the chance to live my dream and play here for so long,” Fleury said. “That’s why it’s always a special place for me to come back.” But before Fleury’s time, there was the back-to-back championship team of the early 1990s featuring star defenseman Larry Murphy. He said hoisting the cup twice is an experience he’ll always remember. “Everything about it, of course, actually getting your hands on the cup, the honor. The skate around the ice with it was something I’ll never forget, but also the reaction of the city of Pittsburgh. It was the first cup for this franchise,” Murphy said, Fans watched a video of Jack McGregor’s vision becoming a reality, as the NHL officially returned to Pittsburgh in 1966 after a 36-year absence. His family accepted his posthumous honor, decades after he helped to lay the groundwork for some of the league’s most talented players and their fans. “I’ll never forget the airport, when we arrived … you really got a sense, right then and there, just how much that meant to the city,” Murphy said. Inductee Jim Rutherford said Pittsburgh is a true sports town, one that he’s honored to have been a part of, serving as the Penguins general manager from 2014-2021. “With the group that we had and the run that we had, it was just one of those, two of those, years that were just a dream come true,” Rutherford said. item.title: No. 6 Texas 22, No. 21 LSU 21: Three things we learned
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Princewill Umanmielen #1 of the Louisiana State Tigers tackles Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns during the first quarter of a game at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an instantly-iconic 22-21 win over the No. 21 LSU Tigers in Baton Rouge, the No. 6 Texas Longhorns pulled ahead with a well-designed four-yard touchdown pass from Arch Manning to Raleek Brown with four seconds remaining to secure a fast-track to the College Football Playoff with two games remaining. Texas may have figured out how to win The clock-management decisions at the end of the game were puzzling, to say the least, but when push came to shove, Texas had its best offensive drive of the game as time expired. When Raleek Brown ran into the end zone to give the Horns the go-ahead touchdown, it felt cathartic after the 2019 game in Austin when a running back dropped a pivotal four-down touchdown pass. When it was time to win, Texas went 58 yards in 12 plays and took all but the final ticks off the clock, coming a week after the Longhorns went on the road and put away a top-25 team decisively. It was ugly. It was frustrating. It was confusing. But when the clock struck zeroes, Texas went into one of the toughest environments in the country and came away with a win, keeping all its goals alive for the year. The offense is the limiting factor We already knew this, so it’s cheating to include it here, but it showed up in prime time against LSU. The Tigers and quarterback Sam Leavitt tried to give the Longhorns the game, but Texas gave it right back. Twice, Texas answered an LSU interception with an interception of its own, both of which led to opposing touchdowns. That was nearly the difference in the game — LSU scored 14 points off turnovers and Texas scored zero. If you flip even one of those empty frames into a touchdown, this is a much different contest. The offensive line struggled with pressures all night, but Steve Sarkisian seemed content to let Arch deal with a collapsing pocket on long-developing plays. They moved far away from the screens and quick game that served them so well against Missouri, and it showed — the offense sputtered and flailed while the defense did its best to hold on. item.title: Former LSU Legend Does What He Just Criticized Ahead of Texas Game
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LA - OCTOBER 10: Leonard Fournette #7 of the LSU Tigers greets fans prior to a game against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Tiger Stadium on October 10, 2015 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) Getty The LSU Tigers had Leonard Fournette alongside Lane Kiffin before Saturday’s home game against Texas, which made for a sight considering what Fournette said six days earlier. The former LSU running back had criticized celebrities joining the team’s pregame entrance. Now, he was part of the walk himself. Video shared by Jon Blau showed Fournette accompanying Kiffin ahead of the Nov. 14 matchup. On its own, an LSU great returning to support the Tigers would hardly require an explanation. Put it next to his comments on the Nov. 8 edition of the 4th & South podcast, though, and there is something to discuss. LSU RB legend Leonard Fournette, who was not a fan of celebrities walking down Tiger Walk last weekend, accompanied Lane Kiffin into the Texas game today. https://t.co/HOqxAspn9m — Jon Blau (@Jon_Blau) November 14, 2026 Leonard Fournette Had Strong Words About LSU’s Celebrity Walk Fournette’s frustration centered on the attention surrounding famous guests joining the team. He specifically mentioned Shaquille O’Neal and Angel Reese, questioning what their presence did to help LSU win football games. His delivery left no doubt about how strongly he felt. “They had Shaq come out, they had Angel Reese come out,” Fournette said. “Angel Reese and Shaq ain’t going to help us out on the football field?” He continued questioning why those guests were coming off the bus with the players. Fournette also made clear that his criticism did not mean he opposed everything Kiffin was doing. His issue was with that particular part of the presentation. “Yes, I love everything Coach Kiffin is doing, but that s*** has to stop,” Fournette said. Fournette’s Appearance Adds a Different Layer to His Criticism There is a distinction here. Fournette played football for LSU, so his connection to the team involves the sport he was discussing. Fans could reasonably view a former Tigers running back joining the entrance differently from guests whose LSU careers came elsewhere. item.title: Jameson Williams Has Hilarious Message After Finding Lost ID in Germany
item.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams is having himself a good time in Germany, and his latest Instagram story might be one of the funniest moments of the team’s overseas trip. With the Lions preparing to face the New England Patriots in Munich on Sunday, Williams took to his Instagram account Saturday to share a photo of an Irish learner permit that apparently had been left behind in a wallet. But rather than simply announcing that he had found someone’s missing identification, Williams decided to have a little fun with the situation. “Aye if u know bro tell em he left his id in uber tellem Waymo got it I need 2k euros for it back,” Williams wrote, adding laughing and ninja emojis. Yes, you read that correctly. Williams jokingly demanded 2,000 euros to return the lost ID, apparently suggesting that whoever misplaced it would have to pay a pretty hefty finder’s fee. Jameson Williams Enjoying His Time in Germany There is no indication Williams was seriously demanding payment, and the Instagram story appears to have been nothing more than a joke. It’s also unclear whether the identification has been returned to its owner. The lighthearted moment comes as Detroit prepares for its international matchup with New England , a game that has brought plenty of excitement for the organization and its fans. Williams, one of the most explosive players on Detroit’s offense, will soon turn his attention back to football as the Lions look to generate more big plays against the Patriots. For now, though, Jamo appears to be enjoying himself overseas. And somewhere out there, one unfortunate traveler might be wondering how their missing ID ended up on an NFL player’s Instagram story.

item.title: 5 major takeaways from Penn State’s blowout win over Minnesota
item.description: That was easily Penn State’s best win of the season. The team had some other high-scoring games earlier in the year, but those were against much weaker out-of-conference opponents. This game against Minnesota was Penn State’s first excellent game against solid competition all year, although things got a bit dicey at the end. The Nittany Lions won 42-14 in a game that was essentially decided in the first few minutes. The defense was excellent as always, and the offense easily had its most impressive performance of the season — although it was aided by some short fields given to it by the defense. The blue and white are well on their way to a Bowl Game appearance and have gotten the season back on track with that win over the Golden Gophers . Now, let’s take a look at what the driving factors of the game were. Setting the tone Penn State went into the game with a clear goal of establishing the run. The offense scored touchdowns on each of its first two possessions, albeit with shortened fields. However, the most impressive part was that the Nittany Lions ran nine plays on those first two drives, and they ran the ball on seven of them. It was a notable switch from the pass-heavy offense that they had to run at different points this season, and it paid off in a big way. Penn State averaged 5.6 yards per carry and took the wind out of Minnesota’s sails almost immediately. It may have taken much longer than expected, but the blue and white finally got the running game figured out.
